Q: Flutter GetX app freezes on startup due to multiple controllers and heavy initialization work A:

Don’t initialize all controllers at startup. Use Get.lazyPut() instead of Get.put().
This way, controllers are created only when the screen is opened, so they are called only when the page is opened.

If you need to preload data, show a splash screen with loading to load everything in advance, and make sure you load only the important data.

Also, check your Hive models there may be an issue there.

Trying these steps should help resolve the problem.

Q: Does function/method overriding occur only when polymorphism is implemented in java? A:

Method overriding and polymorphism are distinct but related things.

Polymorphism occurs in Java when you use an instance of some class C as an instance of a supertype, S, of C. For instance, you pass it as a method argument where an S is required, or assign it to a variable of type S. Particularly so if methods are then invoked on the object as if it were an S. Polymorphism is an aspect of object interactions.

As the term is defined by the JLS, overriding occurs when a class C declares an instance method with the same name and signature, up to type erasure, as an instance method declared by one of its supertypes and visible to C. Method overriding is an aspect of class definitions.

You can have polymorphic behavior involving types that perform no method overriding. You can have method overriding without any instances of the types involved being used polymorphically. However, some method overrides are targeted in part toward polymorphic usage scenarios.

  1. Is overriding considered a subset/type of polymorphism (Runtime Polymorphism)?

No. Overriding is about class definition, whereas polymorphism is about object usage. One of the aspects of Java's style of polymorphism is that instance method invocations are dispatched based on the class of the object on which they are invoked, rather than based on the type of the expression designating that object. This is referred to as "runtime polymorphism", "dynamic binding", or "late binding". This particular aspect of Java polymorphism is meaningful only because Java supports method overriding, but in a language design sense, polymorphism is about more than late binding, and late binding is not even an essential aspect.

  1. Can you have overriding in a program without "using" polymorphism in a practical sense?

Absolutely. Suppose class Sub extends class Super and overrides method int doSomething(int) of Super. If everywhere an instance of Sub is used, it is accessed via an expression of type Sub, then there is no polymorphism involved. Not even when Sub.doSomething() is invoked.

Q: "OSError: Chromium downloadable not found at" when using requests_html module in python A:

I was hit with same issue. After some head breaking found these commands and helped get the issue resolved (Replace the value '1181217' as per your version need. This one worked for me):

For Windows (PowerShell):

PowerShell

$env:PYPPETEER_CHROMIUM_REVISION = '1181217'
pyppeteer-install

For Windows (CMD):

DOS

set PYPPETEER_CHROMIUM_REVISION=1181217
pyppeteer-install

Q: How can I deploy Next js app on cpanel hosting A:

Deploying on cPanel is easy. You can build the static files and in cPanel create node application > create application, run install script there, seeding commands, etc. But there is a downside to this approach, as some attacker can send a tailored HTTP request and get back a build response and in that response your env data will be visible and this also gets logged to Strader. Logs to your domain/Strader. Logs will give logs with env files so nextjs is not recommended for cPanel hosting from my experience.

Q: How to declare a data member reference in tclOO A:

Donal has answered your question, but there is another way to do it.

oo::class create TestClass {
    variable varRef
    constructor args {
        lassign $args varRef
    }

    method getRefToVar {} {
        upvar 0 $varRef refToVar
        return $refToVar
    }

    method setRefToVar {value} {
        upvar 0 $varRef refToVar
        set refToVar $value
    }
}

Here, you supply the TestClass object with the qualified name of the variable, like ::x for the global variable x, or ::foobar::x for the x variable in the foobar namespace. You save this name in the instance variable varRef.

When you want to read from or write to this variable, you first create a local reference to it:

upvar 0 $varRef refToVar

This means that in the method where you are invoking this command, refToVar is a reference or alias to the variable whose name is stored in varRef.

You can do the same thing in a command procedure:

proc testProc {varRef} {
    upvar 0 $varRef refToVar
    set refToVar 5
}

Testing it:

puts "start"
set x 100
puts $x

puts "proc test"
testProc ::x
puts $x

puts "tclOO test"
TestClass create tst ::x
puts [tst getRefToVar]
tst setRefToVar 20
puts [tst getRefToVar]
puts $x

Note how the names are written differently.

If you somehow don't know the qualified name of the variable, this should be helpful:

TestClass create tst [namespace which -variable x]

BTW: you don't have to write

string range $varRef 1 [expr [string length $varRef] -1]

there is an abbreviated form for that:

string range $varRef 1 end

but you don't have to write that either: to remove zero or more dollar signs from the left end of a string, just

string trimleft $varRef \$

but you don't have to write that either: you don't need to add the dollar sign when passing a variable name:

proc bump varName {
    upvar 1 $varName var
    incr var
}
set x 10
# => 10
bump x
set x
# => 11

Documentation: expr, incr, lassign, namespace, proc, puts, set, string, upvar

Q: Marking-up argument names in comments of functions A:

The proper way to document anything in code is to use tools and their standards. A failure to use a tool, means you are missing on automated validation it provides. Often a tool is built into language, making the choice easy.

In Java - Javadoc, in C++ - Doxygen, in Python use format of your IDE:

  • Plain
  • Epytext
  • reStructuredText
  • Numpy
  • Google

Other languages and environments lead to other natural choices.

The only exception are prototypes and throwaways - documentation is unnecessary for unsupported code.
